title: Implement panelized GF(2^m) GEMM
description:
Reduce per-output-cell scratch/export overhead with panelized multi-output GEMM.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] GF(2^m) GEMM target rows are within 1.5x of the selected reference or faster, scoped per-cell by the maturity markers below.
- [hard] The scalar fallback and existing CLMUL batch path remain correct.

## Amendment - 2026-05-06 (user-approved, Path A)

Per AskUserQuestion 2026-05-06 (e24f7839 closure), criterion #1 is amended to permit per-cell maturity-marker scoping. Empirical basis is the e24f7839 panelized-GEMM evidence (`dev/bench_results/2026-05-06-e24f7839-panelized-gf2m-gemm.md`).

Per-cell maturity markers:
- GF(2^32) at n in {64, 256, 1024}: [hard] PASS (5.7x-6.7x of NTL on Zen-3 — measurements in `2026-05-06-e24f7839-gf2pow32-panelized.csv`)
- GF(2^16) at n in {64, 256}: [hard] PASS (35.6x-148.5x of M4RIE — already passing pre-panelization, improved by panelization)
- GF(2^16) at n=1024: [aspirational] (ratio 0.614, 8.5% below 0.667 threshold; close to single-core VPCLMULQDQ ceiling at the 3-CLMUL Barrett chain depth. Closing requires GFNI or AVX-512 ZMM, neither available on Zen-3 host class. Per fb271c41 decision, those are documented as future direction for Zen-4+ hosts.)
- GF(2^8) at n in {64, 256, 1024}: [aspirational] (M4RIE uses O(n^3/log n) Newton-John / Method of Four Russians with byte-level table lookups; gf2-core panelized GEMM is O(n^3) per-element CLMUL. Closing the gap requires a different algorithm class — distinct work from this issue's scope.)

The deeper GF(2^m) algorithmic catch-up (including GF(2^8) Newton-John / Method of Four Russians) is owned by the broader finite-field SOTA catch-up plan in issue `615db3b9` (`dev/active/615db3b9-finite-field-la-sota-plan.md`), not duplicated as a separate follow-up under this story.

Re-escalation threshold: re-escalate to user when (a) `615db3b9` breakdown lands a Newton-John GF(2^8) sub-issue and that closes (revisit GF(2^8) cells), (b) GFNI/AVX-512 lane is harnessed for Zen-4+ host class (revisit GF(2^16) n=1024).
